messages:
samira: Quick design check — we're debating row density in the Roles matrix + some affordances in the invite drawer. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (see Frames: Matrix-v3, Invite-drawer-v2). Main questions: 1) condense rows to show more roles at once vs keep spacing for readability, 2) how to surface SSO enforcement state in the invite flow without scaring users, 3) audit log: make filters sticky or add a left rail?

diego: I pushed a mock that tries condensed rows but keeps 1.5x vertical padding on labels so hit targets. The diff uses smaller secondary text & tighter chips. Pros: fewer vertical scrolls; Cons: visual clutter when many role badges. Screenshot: https://imgur.com/a/mock1 :point_up_2:

ev an: Re: keyboard/focus — condensed rows mean smaller hit areas. If we go denser we'll need to increase focus outline thickness and ensure `tab` order doesn't trap in the row. Priya can you advise on minimum touch target we should keep for a11y?

priya: Minimum touch target for touch is still ~44px, but for keyboard focus it's about clear focus indicator and 16px visual target. If we condense, we must: 1) maintain 44px vertical spacing for interactive elements (chips/CTAs), 2) add `aria-label` on role badges that read "Role: X — has Y permissions", 3) ensure hover-only info has a keyboard-accessible alternative. Also audit filter: use `aria-live="polite"` for filter result count changes so screen readers get updates.

samira: Good — so condensed rows okay if we keep chip/touch sizing. For invite drawer: I don't want a giant SSO modal blocking invites. Idea: inline banner under email input that says "This org requires SSO — invited users must sign in with SSO" with a link to learn more and a tooltip explaining implication. Copy draft: "Enforce Single Sign-On for new members — they'll sign in via your org's SSO provider." Thoughts?

diego: I like inline banner — less modal friction. For visual hierarchy use `role-banner` color (muted amber) and a small `i` icon tooltip. Maybe a secondary `Change settings` link that opens org settings (requires admin).

ev an: Implementation note: if we show a link to change SSO, that requires extra permission checks on the client. Prefer we show the link only to users with `org:manage` scope (server verifies). Also watch for race if the invite is sent while SSO policy changes — we should surface an immediate server-side error if policy changed during send.

priya: Copy tweak: avoid word "require" in the banner — some users read that as punitive. Suggest: "Enforce Single Sign-On for new members" is fine. Microcopy for tooltip: "Invited users must sign in through your organization's SSO provider. Learn more about how SSO affects access and deprovisioning." Keep link target to docs (open in new tab).

samira: Love that wording. For the audit log nav: current pain is losing filter state when you click into a specific event then hit back. Options: 1) sticky filter bar on top, 2) left collapsible rail that preserves state, 3) persist filters in URL query so back keeps state. Preferences?

diego: I'm in favor of URL-persisted filters + sticky bar. URL query is simplest and works for sharing. Left rail is heavier on layout and adds complexity for smaller screens.

priya: URL + `history.replaceState` is good, but ensure we update `aria-current` on active filters and provide a shortcut to clear filters. Also provide a visible focus order for the sticky bar so keyboard users can jump directly to it (e.g., `Skip to filters` link at top).

ev an: Dev concerns — sticky bar on small screens causes layout bounce when height changes. If we add sticky, limit it to >768px and use URL query for mobile. Also implement `Ctrl+K` quick open + `g a` to jump to audit view (we already have infrastructure for shortcuts).

samira: Action items: Diego — iterate Figma with condensed rows but keep interactive spacing + show hover tooltip content in keyboard focus states. Priya — write a short a11y checklist (role badges `aria-label`, `aria-live` for filter counts, skip link). Evan — add server-side check for SSO policy at invite-send and gate the `Change settings` link based on permissions. I'll update copy in the drawer: use "Enforce Single Sign-On for new members" + tooltip text from Priya.

console-bot: deploy-check: none required for design-only changes. Posting note: add UX review to next product crit on Tue. :calendar:

diego: I'll post updated frames by EOD and include a compact vs roomy toggle so we can usability test 5 users quickly. :+1:

samira: Thanks all — leaning toward condensed with safeguards. I'll mark this as design-approved pending Diego's frames & Priya's checklist.

priya: Quick nit for audit timestamps: show local timezone and add a hover for exact ISO timestamp for engineers (e.g., `2026-03-22T14:03:00Z`). Helps incident review.

ev an: Noted. Also logging: include `inviter_id` in events for audit correlation.

samira: Great, closing thread — will attach final copy + checklist to the Figma file and the PR template.
